news.Title: Intel Just Landed Its First 18A-P Chip Customer. What That Means for INTC Stock.
news.Content:
Intel (INTC) has long been a prominent name in the semiconductor industry, supplying processors for personal computers and data centers. Its stock, however, has had a difficult run, losing more than half its value since the end of September.

Sentiment deteriorated further late last month after management warned that quarterly revenue could fall at least $1 billion short of analyst expectations, blaming weaker PC demand and ongoing supply chain disruptions.

More News from Barchart

'We Don't Want That Much Failure': Late Billionaire Charlie Munger Said Elon Musk 'Likes Taking on the Impossible Job,' Berkshire Looks for 'The Easy Job'

A $150 Billion Reason to Buy the Nvidia Stock Dip

Leadership Risk vs. Record Numbers: Nvidia Posted $115 Billion in Revenue in Its First Report Without Jensen Huang. What It Means for NVDA Stock.

Markets move fast. Keep up by reading our FREE midday Barchart Brief newsletter for exclusive charts, analysis, and headlines.

Against this backdrop, CEO Lip-Bu Tan delivered a much-needed positive development on Wednesday, Nov. 18, announcing that Intel had secured its first external customer for its 18A process node. The 18A platform sits at the heart of Intel's ambitions to become a serious competitor in advanced semiconductor manufacturing.

Described as a 1.8-nanometer-class process, the technology is designed to support increasingly sophisticated chips for artificial intelligence (AI), high-performance computing, and major cloud infrastructure providers. However, developing advanced technology is only half the challenge.

Intel has committed tens of billions of dollars to expanding and modernizing its manufacturing capabilities. Without third-party customers, the investment could remain heavily dependent on Intel's own chip designs.

Therefore, success in this area could help Intel compete more directly with industry leader Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSM) for some of the market's most valuable manufacturing contracts.

About Intel Stock

The Santa Clara, California-based Intel Corporation designs, develops, manufactures, and markets processors, graphics chips, and advanced computing solutions. Its portfolio spans CPUs for personal computers and commercial devices, GPUs, server processors, AI accelerators, networking components, and data center technologies.

With a market cap of nearly $290.6 billion, its operations extend beyond chip design, with semiconductor manufacturing, wafer fabrication, autonomous driving technologies, and advanced packaging solutions also part of its business.

Story Continues

On the price-performance front, INTC stock is up 62% over the past 52 weeks and 47% year-to-date (YTD), but the recent slide has taken some shine off those gains. Shares have dropped 41% in a month, as manufacturing delays, tougher competition, and sluggish PC demand continue to test Intel's turnaround, as its latest earnings made clear.

Valuation adds another layer to the discussion. INTC stock is currently trading at 36.77 times forward adjusted earnings and 4.71 times sales. Both multiples are above industry averages, suggesting the stock commands a premium despite its recent correction.

Surpasses Q3 Earnings

Intel's Q3 FY2026 results, released on Oct. 29, offered plenty of financial positives, although the market reaction was anything but encouraging. Shares initially declined 3.6% on the announcement date before suffering a much steeper 28.6% drop in the following trading session.

Net sales increased 20.9% year-over-year (YoY) to $16.5 billion, extending a notable run of revenue outperformance. For the eighth consecutive quarter, actual revenue exceeded management's expectations. It also topped analysts' estimates of $16.42 billion.

Non-GAAP gross margin expanded to 44.1%, while non-GAAP operating margin climbed to 19.6%. Non-GAAP net income jumped 169.4% from its year-ago level to $2.8 billion, and non-GAAP EPS surged 126.1% YoY to $0.52, surpassing the $0.40 Street estimate.

Much of this strength came from Data Center and AI (DCAI), which emerged as the standout growth engine. Revenue in the division surged 78% YoY to $7.3 billion, supported by stronger demand from hyperscalers, enterprise customers, and neocloud providers. Increasing CPU requirements for AI infrastructure and agentic workloads provided an important tailwind for the segment.

Yet, the impressive demand figures also exposed a problem that the chipmaker has struggled to resolve. Advanced packaging shortages and manufacturing constraints continue to restrict shipments, leaving the business unable to fully translate customer demand into delivered products.

The picture was less encouraging in Client Computing and Physical AI (CCPG), where revenue declined 5% from the corresponding period last year to $8.1 billion. Higher memory prices, tighter IT budgets, and inventory reductions among original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) continued to pressure PC demand, making this division a notable weak spot in an otherwise stronger quarter.

Elsewhere, Intel Foundry delivered one of the more encouraging performances, with revenue climbing 58% YoY to $6.7 billion. Financial flexibility also improved, as adjusted free cash flow rose 92.9% YoY to $1.7 billion.

Looking ahead, management expects Q4 revenue to range between $15 billion and $16 billion. Its guidance also calls for a non-GAAP gross margin of 38% and non-GAAP EPS of $0.25, indicating the next quarter could see a moderation in profitability even as the business navigates supply constraints.

Analysts, meanwhile, anticipate Q4 FY2026 EPS of $0.15, up 275% YoY. The full-year FY2026 estimate stands at $1.04, reflecting 966.7% growth from the previous year. Further out, the FY2027 EPS forecast of $1.31 points to a 26% increase from the prior year.

What Do Analysts Expect for INTC Stock?

Despite the recent share-price setback, Wall Street's overall stance on Intel remains "Hold." Of the 46 analysts covering INTC stock, nine have assigned a "Strong Buy" rating, one maintains a "Moderate Buy," and 35 recommend "Hold," while one analyst has issued a "Strong Sell" rating.

The average price target currently stands at $92.67, suggesting potential upside of 72%. Meanwhile, the Street-high target of $160 indicates a possible gain of 197% from current levels.

news.Title: Intel announces more layoffs as workforce shrinks by 7,300
news.Content:
Strong earnings are no longer a guarantee of job security, even for employees at some of America's largest technology companies.

The artificial intelligence boom has fueled demand for advanced processors and data-center infrastructure, encouraging semiconductor manufacturers to invest billions of dollars in additional production capacity.

But those investments are also taking place alongside efforts to restructure operations, reduce costs and compete more effectively in the AI race.

Intel is among the companies pursuing a leaner workforce despite improving business performance.

The California-based semiconductor giant reported a 21% increase in third-quarter revenue in October, driven by a 78% surge in its Data Center and AI business.

Yet the company continues to eliminate jobs.

Intel has disclosed plans to permanently cut another 57 positions across its Santa Clara facilities, according to a Nov. 16 Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification (WARN) notice reviewed by TheStreet.

The latest reductions come as Intel's reported global workforce has shrunk by 7,300 employees over the past year, even as CEO Lip-Bu Tan works to rebuild the company's standing in the semiconductor industry.

Intel discloses another round of California layoffs

In its November WARN, Intel disclosed plans to permanently eliminate approximately 57 positions across four Santa Clara facilities.

The affected locations include its Robert Noyce Building at 2200 Mission College Boulevard and three additional facilities identified as SC-9, SC-11 and SC-12.

According to the notice, the first separations were scheduled to occur during a 14-day period beginning Nov. 15.

Intel's California layoffs disclosed between July and November 2026

The latest reductions follow three earlier notices filed between July and October, covering Intel's operations in Santa Clara and Folsom.

The documents show that the reductions extend into some of Intel's engineering and technical operations.

The latest November filing includes a breakdown of the 57 affected positions.

At the Robert Noyce Building, 33 workers are affected, including 5 infrastructure and DevOps engineers, 3 software application development engineers, 2 security research engineers or scientists, and several other technical and administrative employees.

Story Continues

More Layoffs:

Canva CEO apologizes to workers, makes unusual promise amid layoffs

Disney eyes thousands more layoffs as major cost-cutting push widens

Popular website builder cuts 19% of jobs as CEO signals major shift

Another 19 positions are affected at SC-12, including 5 platform hardware design engineers, four electronic design automation tools hardware engineers and two physical design engineers.

The remaining 5 positions are spread across SC-9 and SC-11.

The October notice covering Intel's Folsom campus also identifies substantial reductions in engineering roles, including product development engineers, engineering managers, and software specialists.

The filings do not identify particular projects being discontinued or indicate that any of the affected facilities are closing.

According to Intel's latest Form 10-Q filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission , employee severance and benefit-related charges totaled $290 million during the first nine months of 2026.

That included $55 million in the third quarter alone.

Related: Boeing's 2,500 job cuts come with a troubling unanswered question

What Intel is offering affected employees

The WARN notices provide details about the support being offered to employees losing their jobs.

The company said affected workers were either being notified of their separations at least 60 days in advance or receiving shorter notice accompanied by nine weeks of pay and benefits in lieu of additional notice.

Under the October Folsom notice, the shorter notification period was approximately two weeks, compared with approximately four weeks in the Santa Clara notices.

Intel has also partnered with career transition firm Lee Hecht Harrison to provide outplacement and retraining services for up to 6 months.

The services include personal career coaching, résumé and LinkedIn profile support, interview preparation, job-search assistance and professional development resources.

The notices state that the affected employees are not represented by a union and do not have the right to displace other employees from their positions.

The documents do not establish Intel's total worldwide layoffs for November or indicate whether additional reductions are planned beyond those identified in the filings.

Intel workforce shrinks despite stronger earnings

The latest cuts come amid a multiyear contraction in Intel's workforce.

According to the company's third-quarter earnings release , Intel had approximately 81,100 employees worldwide as of Sept. 26, 2026, including workers at Mobileye and other subsidiaries.

That compares with 88,400 a year earlier, representing a decline of 7,300 employees, or approximately 8.3%.

How Intel's global workforce has changed

Intel's reported workforce has fallen much further since the end of 2024.

The figures represent an overall decline of approximately 27,800 employees since December 2024, although that total should not be interpreted as the number of people laid off.

Employee departures, hiring activity and business divestitures have all influenced the company's reported headcount.

The shrinking workforce illustrates the scale of Intel's restructuring over the past two years.

Meanwhile, its latest financial results suggest that some of those efforts are taking place alongside a substantial business recovery.

Intel generated $16.5 billion in third-quarter revenue , compared with $13.7 billion a year earlier.

Its Data Center and AI division reported revenue of $7.3 billion, up 78% year over year, as demand for server processors continued to accelerate.

Chief Financial Officer David Zinsner said the quarter marked the company's strongest data-center revenue growth in 15 years.

However, the recovery remains uneven.

Intel's Client Computing and Physical AI business reported a 5% decline in revenue, while its foundry division continued operating at a loss.

The company reported $3.3 billion in GAAP net income attributable to Intel, down 18% from the previous year, despite its higher revenue.

Intel also forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion, below the third quarter's $16.5 billion, as weakness in the PC market and supply constraints continued to affect its outlook.

Intel CEO acknowledges dramatic workforce restructuring

During Intel's October 29 earnings call , Tan discussed the scale of the changes undertaken during the company's restructuring.

He described the progress as including "a dramatic resizing of our workforce, eliminating middle management and bureaucracy, streamlining our executive ranks"

Tan also said Intel had established a largely new leadership team and worked to restore an engineering-focused culture.

"We still have much more to do," he said.

The remarks came as the company continued to invest in manufacturing technology and expand capacity to support growing demand for its processors.

Tan said Intel's server business was experiencing particularly strong demand from customers building AI infrastructure.

CFO Zinsner also acknowledged that demand for the company's Data Center and AI products continued to exceed available supply.

Intel expects capital expenditures and purchasing commitments to rise over the coming quarters as it attempts to address those supply constraints.

The contrast reflects the company's restructuring strategy: Intel is reducing staffing and management costs in some areas while directing capital toward manufacturing capabilities and products it considers central to its future growth.

Although AI-related demand is helping drive Intel's investment decisions, the company has not attributed the reductions to AI automation.

Intel's recovery follows years of financial struggles

For decades, Intel was one of the dominant names in the semiconductor industry, helping power the personal computer revolution and supplying processors for servers around the world.

Unlike companies that primarily design chips and outsource their production, Intel built its business around developing and manufacturing its own processors.

But it came under increasing pressure as competitors gained ground in chip design and advanced manufacturing.

Nvidia emerged as a dominant supplier of processors used in artificial intelligence systems, while AMD strengthened its position in personal-computer and server chips.

Meanwhile, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co., which manufactures chips for other companies, advanced its production technologies as Intel struggled with delays in its own manufacturing processes.

Intel acknowledged those difficulties in its 2025 annual report .

The company said delays in developing new manufacturing technologies had allowed competitors using TSMC to benefit from advanced processes introduced ahead of Intel.

It also acknowledged that it had "missed the significant shift in compute demand to GPUs optimized for AI workloads."

That failure was costly.

Intel recorded approximately $922 million in inventory-related charges tied to its Gaudi AI accelerators in 2024 and another $375 million in 2025.

In August 2024, then-CEO Pat Gelsinger announced plans to eliminate roughly 15,000 positions as part of a cost-reduction initiative intended to deliver $10 billion in savings in 2025.

Gelsinger departed later that year, and Tan became CEO in March 2025.

Under Tan, Intel intensified efforts to reduce management layers, simplify operations and concentrate investment on its core client and server businesses.

The company's annual GAAP net loss narrowed to approximately $300 million in 2025, while several business segments have reported improving performance in 2026.

But Intel has not fully recovered its former position.

Its foundry division, which manufactures semiconductors, reported approximately $6.7 billion in revenue for the third quarter of 2026, up 58% year over year.

However, much of that revenue came from transactions within Intel's own operations. The foundry business still recorded an operating loss of approximately $1.9 billion during the quarter.

The company's ongoing investments in advanced manufacturing therefore remain a significant part of its longer-term turnaround strategy.

news.Title: Bank of America sends strong signal to Microsoft stock investors
news.Content:
Microsoft has spent years building toward an enterprise AI moment it believed was coming.

The infrastructure it bet on was not a model. It was Office: a user base built up over decades, their documents, their email histories, and the workflows running through all of it.

Copilot is the product now sitting on top of that base.

Bank of America analyst Tal Liani hosted an investor session with Jacob Andreou, executive vice president of Copilot, on Nov. 20. The setup was different from a standard earnings call. Liani brought Andreou directly in front of investors to walk through where the enterprise AI strategy stands, what Microsoft is still building, and what it still needs to prove.

Liani reiterated a Buy rating on Microsoft (MSFT) with a price target of $630, against a Nov. 20 closing price of $498.30. In a note shared with TheStreet, he laid out the case Andreou made and what it means for investors watching the stock.

Why enterprise AI still depends on context more than capability

Andreou's starting point was a problem Microsoft has been pitching for a while. Frontier models score well on benchmarks. Put them inside a company with no access to its files, client histories, or the conversations employees have been having for years, and the results start to disappoint.

Also read: Microsoft CEO Nadella faces uncomfortable reality after outage

Andreou called Work IQ Copilot's intelligence layer. He described how it tracks the way work actually moves inside an organization: an email thread about a client deal, the Teams call that followed it, the files that came out of that call, all linked together. When a question touches any part of that chain, the system is built to pull it up.

The outside providers have capable models. Getting those models to understand a specific company's internal work, its email threads, project history, and files going back years, requires access Microsoft already has.

Andreou made that case at the session. The note put it at the center of Copilot's competitive position.

3 tiers and what they tell investors about how revenue scales

Andreou described three types of users, each with a different revenue profile. Starters already have basic Copilot features inside their Microsoft 365 plans. They're using the product, just not paying for it separately. Getting them to eventually buy a seat is the first conversion Microsoft is after.

Subscribers are paying for a Copilot seat. The more engaged users go further, into modules like Autopilot for background task execution, Code for building custom apps and dashboards, and Cowork for working across multiple files at once. Those modules bill on consumption, meaning Microsoft charges based on what the system actually processes.

Story Continues

Both moves matter for where the revenue goes. Getting Starters to pay for a Copilot seat is one path. Getting paying subscribers to actually use the consumption modules is a different bet entirely.

The note put both as necessary for the paid seat growth Liani's Buy rating assumes.

What keeps enterprise customers inside Microsoft's ecosystem

Andreou's third line of argument was harder to put a number on. Organizations that bring in Copilot don't have to reorganize how they work. Word stays Word. Teams stays Teams. Someone who hasn't adopted Copilot at all still opens the same files from the same folders as everyone else around them.

For companies trying to displace Microsoft in enterprise software , that's key. Pulling an organization off Office means moving document storage, file sharing, security controls, and compliance workflows at the same time, through legal, IT, and security teams simultaneously.

The note put that barrier among the three main structural advantages Copilot brings to competition with outside AI providers.

More Microsoft:

Microsoft's Windows sales fell 22% as PC prices climb

Microsoft CEO sees a problem ahead for AI stock investors

Microsoft just gave Nvidia shareholders a reason to pay attention

Copilot Workspaces, launched at Ignite , runs on the same premise. A team gets a shared space to run work through Copilot. The person in the organization who hasn't adopted the tool still accesses the same documents under the same security controls.

Andreou said that was intentional. The product is built to function without a full company rollout behind it.

Microsoft's pricing structure and what Bank of America is betting on

Pricing came up near the end of the session. Andreou laid out a flat monthly rate for everyday Copilot use and a separate consumption meter for heavier tasks.

The note said Microsoft structured it that way so companies can roll the product out broadly without committing upfront to a budget that depends on predicting how much people will use it.

Auto mode runs inside the consumption tier and handles model selection automatically. It routes each step in a task to whatever fits: lower-cost models for simpler work, more capable ones when the task gets heavier.

Andreou also raised a broader issue during the session: AI products still require users to know what to ask. The Today feature, rolled out at Ignite, pushes relevant work to users before they ask for it.

Liani's $630 price target is built on 28 times his calendar year 2027 earnings estimate, a premium to the peer group range of 18 to 25 times. He wrote in the note that Microsoft's revenue growth and margin profile justify paying above that range.

At $498.30, the target implies roughly 26% upside. He also listed three downside risks: gross margin pressure as Azure scales, faster AI innovation from outside Microsoft, and a slowdown in enterprise application spending.

The last of those is the one most enterprise AI bulls are not modeling.

news.Title: Why Saturday’s Historic Starship Catch Changes the Bull Case for SpaceX Stock
news.Content:
This past weekend was a big one for the space sector, with Space Exploration Technologies (NASDAQ:SPCX) showing it's light-years ahead of its competition. For the first time, SpaceX successfully caught the upper stage of its Starship rocket using mechanical arms attached to its launch tower. It was a major milestone for the company, setting the stage for its future space ambitions.

Also this weekend, rival United Launch Alliance (ULA), a joint venture between Boeing (NYSE:BA) and Lockheed Martin (NYSE:LMT), had a major setback. Its Vulcan rocket failed, destroying 40 Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) Leo satellites in the process.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

This weekend's results show the growing distance that SpaceX is gaining over its competitors in the space sector. Its achievement also comes months after Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket exploded on the ground in May, destroying the company's only launch pad. Space competitors are clearly struggling with launches, which is also hurting Amazon's efforts to get its Leo satellite internet service, which will compete with Amazon's Starlink, off the ground.

Still, not everything went well for SpaceX this weekend. It decided to abandon trying to catch Starship's Super Heavy booster, which it diverted to the Gulf of Mexico, where it exploded before reaching the water.

The Super Heavy Booster is the much more expensive part of Starship. According to PayLoad Research, a Starship rocket costs around $90 million, with the Super Heavy booster making up about $63 million of the total. However, the Super Heavy Booster is the easier part of the rocket to catch, and SpaceX has already caught it on its own multiple times.

Image source: SpaceX.

A space monopoly

Having a fully reusable rocket is paramount for SpaceX to achieve some of its loftier goals, like orbital data centers and Earth-to-Earth cargo transport. By rapidly reusing a $90 million rocket multiple times rather than just once, SpaceX not only saves a lot of money but also greatly increases the number of launches it can perform.

This completely changes the economics of space and sets the company up for strong growth and the ability to disrupt industries, essentially shifting SpaceX's space segment from being a low-margin launch business into a scalable logistics business, where fuel and maintenance are the main recurring costs.

Story Continues

It also positions SpaceX as a monopoly in the orbital economy. By being the only company with massive, rapidly reusable rockets, SpaceX would control the entire market. It could price its services below competitors to win deals and capture the bulk of the market, while its huge cost advantage would allow it to pocket strong margins. Meanwhile, it would have a huge structural advantage that would allow it to build out Starlink or orbital data centers at costs well below competitors that would have to pay retail launch prices.

SpaceX still faces obstacles to achieving some of its loftier goals. It doesn't matter if SpaceX can launch data centers into space at a cost much lower than competitors' if it can't overcome some important hurdles.

One obstacle it will need to overcome is getting chips that can withstand cosmic radiation, which can flip bits and corrupt data. It is currently working with Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) on a solution. It also needs to be able to develop a cooling solution, as currently there is no way to cool these systems in the vacuum of space. Meanwhile, with Earth-to-Earth transport, it will need to get past a lot of political red tape to launch rockets from places like China to the U.S.

Overall, this past weekend helped put SpaceX in the driver's seat and gave investors another reason to get excited about the stock. While it still has hurdles to overcome before entering some exciting new markets, its lead just keeps growing. That makes this growth stock a buy.

news.Title: Top bank resets Tesla stock target, yet standalone value is alarming
news.Content: Wall Street ended a bruising week on Friday, November 20, as the deepening AI stock rout pushed the S&P 500 into correction territory and wiped out the Nasdaq's gains for the entire year, as reported by Yahoo Finance . Caught squarely in the crosshairs was Tesla ( TSLA ), which took a big hit alongside Silicon Valley's biggest names as nervous investors dumped several high-multiple growth stocks. Interestingly, the stock's slide happened on the very same day one of Wall Street's biggest Tesla skeptics finally blinked. In a November 20 note, HSBC analyst Michael Tyndall upgraded the stock from Reduce to Hold and more than doubled his 12-month price target. Yet beneath that headline reversal, the math tells a far more unsettling story. Inside HSBC's $359 reset, and the alarming $212 standalone floor underneath Tyndall's note switched up how HSBC values the $1.37 trillion automaker. More Tesla: Tesla stock sellers should pump their brakes, 5-star analyst says Bank of America resets Tesla forecast as Robotaxi miles double Tesla wants to sell a car with no steering wheel this year Previously, the bank anchored its bearish stance on Tesla's core operations , noting that third quarter sales hit $28.05 billion ($20.56 billion from autos) and free cash flow reached $1.53 billion, even as U.S. electric vehicle demand cooled after the $7,500 federal tax credit expired and China's market share narrowed. That said, in the note HSBC nudged its standalone discounted cash flow valuation up only slightly, from $193 to $212 per share. Against Tesla's November 19 closing price of $374.41, that implied 43.4% downside; even after Friday's drop to $345.82, it still represents a 38.7% haircut. To arrive at his $359, Tyndall split his valuation 50/50, layering that $212 standalone figure with a hypothetical SpaceX takeover ( SPCX ) at $507 per share, which assumes a hefty 33% acquisition premium over Tesla's trailing 30-day average price. Ironically, Friday's rout pushed Tesla slightly behind HSBC's new target (+3.8% upside), even though $359 suggested downside at the time. What Elon Musk really wants from a SpaceX–Tesla merger Deal talk is far from being simply idle speculation. On October 20 , Elon Musk confirmed that both companies had formed special committees of independent directors to explore a combination, with Bloomberg reporting that an announcement could arrive as early as December or early 2027. Speaking at the New York Times DealBook Summit on Nov. 18, Musk talked about the growing overlap in AI, robotics, and chip design, Story Continues "You don't need them to be together, but would they be better together? I mean, probably, yes." Addressing pay concerns, he added: "I should not receive those stock option awards simply for merging with SpaceX because that is not meeting the deal, which was that I should only get those stock options for Tesla performance, not just because of a merger." That said, HSBC isn't blindly buying into the synergy pitch. Tyndall notes that the strategic benefits appear limited as the two companies serve entirely different customers and already share chip work through their Terafab joint venture. Instead, he pointed straight to governance: "We see control as the key motivation for a merger, especially as CEO Musk has been clear in the past about his need for oversight." as reported by Investing . The math is what's most revealing. Musk holds nearly 39% of SpaceX, wielding 70% of voting power via 10-vote Class B stock, compared to roughly 20% of Tesla (19.8% according to proxy filings), and HSBC estimates he would hold roughly 60% voting power in a combined giant. Tesla's $45.45 billion cash-and-investments cushion and over $20 billion annual capex could ease SpaceX's cash burn after it spent $48.07 billion on nine months of capex and issued $32 billion in bonds yielding over 8% for Nvidia chips, as reported by Yahoo Finance . Why Wall Street is divided over a Tesla-SpaceX merger HSBC's $359 Tesla price target is significantly below Wall Street's consensus estimate of $417.31, but analysts are clearly divided over whether a SpaceX merger would actually benefit Tesla shareholders. Some see enormous upside. Popular Tesla bull Dan Ives puts the chances of a deal by late 2027 at 80% to 90% and argues that Tesla could trade above $500, as covered by Yahoo Finance . Meanwhile, RBC analyst Tom Narayan outlined a potential all-stock deal valuing Tesla at $480 per share, paving the way for a $3.74 trillion company. Under that scenario, Tesla shareholders could potentially own 48% of the combined business, while SpaceX shareholders would own 52%. Others remain a lot less convinced. On November 20, Future Fund's Gary Black warned Tesla shares could initially jump on a merger announcement, only to fall as investors rush to sell. He argues that a proposed 24% deal premium might quickly disappear, potentially dragging Tesla stock toward $280 within a month. There's another major hurdle. Tesla would reportedly need approval from holders of at least 50% of its outstanding shares. That means shareholders who decide not to vote could effectively count against the deal. For everyday investors, HSBC's warning comes down to one uncomfortable number: $212 . That's the bank's estimate of Tesla's value on its own, without a SpaceX deal. If the merger never happens, investors might be left holding a stock priced far above HSBC's estimate of its standalone value. news.Title: Jeff Bezos predicts Amazon will eventually 'go bankrupt' and shares 30-year rule behind it
news.Content:
Founders usually talk about their companies like proud parents at a graduation. One of the richest men on the planet once stood in front of his own staff and talked about the funeral.

Amazon founder Jeff Bezos gave that answer when an employee asked where the company was headed. He said Amazon would one day go under, and he had a number in mind for how long giants like it usually last.

"Amazon is not too big to fail," Bezos said at an all-hands meeting in Seattle in November 2018, according to a recording heard by CNBC . "In fact, I predict one day Amazon will fail. Amazon will go bankrupt. If you look at large companies, their lifespans tend to be 30-plus years, not a hundred-plus years."

That's the 30-year rule, and Bezos applied it to his own company.

More Bezos: Warren Buffett told Jeff Bezos the real reason people don't just 'copy' his investing strategy to get rich

Sears had just proved Bezos' point

The employee's question was about what Amazon could learn from recent retail bankruptcies like Sears, according to CNBC . The 132-year-old chain had filed for Chapter 11 weeks earlier, in October 2018. Toys "R" Us had shuttered its last U.S. stores that June.

Amazon was 24 at the time, founded in July 1994. By Bezos' own math, the company was already most of the way to its expiration date.

The data backs up his gloomy math. Companies on the S&P 500 in the late 1970s stayed on the index for an average of 30 to 35 years, according to growth strategy firm Innosight , which forecast that the figure would shrink to 15 to 20 years this decade.

Amazon's goal was never to live forever

So Amazon is mortal. So what? Bezos' answer was that the job isn't avoiding the end. It's pushing it back.

He told employees to "obsess over customers," according to CNBC.

"If we start to focus on ourselves, instead of focusing on our customers, that will be the beginning of the end," Bezos said. "We have to try and delay that day for as long as possible."

He had already spelled out what happens when a company stops doing that.

"Day 2 is stasis," Bezos wrote in his 2016 letter to shareholders , published in April 2017. "Followed by irrelevance. Followed by excruciating, painful decline. Followed by death. And that is why it is always Day 1."

Day 1 meant acting like a startup that has to earn every customer, even at a company Amazon's size. In the same letter, Bezos pointed to Prime as proof. "No customer ever asked Amazon to create the Prime membership program, but it sure turns out they wanted it," he wrote.

Story Continues

The approach is still paying off. Amazon turned 32 in July, already past the line Bezos drew, and on June 3, it took the No. 1 spot on the Fortune 500 for the first time. It ended Walmart's 13-year run after bringing in $716.9 billion in 2025 revenue. When Amazon first made the list just over two decades ago, it ranked No. 492.

Jeff Bezos says your family is 'not going to need' 2 paychecks thanks to AI

Bill Gates warns of 'winners and losers' over next 20 years, even in 'very best case'

Elon Musk says Larry Page's 'Five Nines' AI prediction is right, despite their decade-long feud

Bezos handed the stopwatch to Andy Jassy

On Feb. 2, 2021, Bezos announced he was giving up the top job.

"I'm excited to announce that this Q3 I'll transition to Executive Chair of the Amazon Board and Andy Jassy will become CEO," Bezos wrote in an email to employees .

He called running Amazon "a deep responsibility, and it's consuming," and added that "this isn't about retiring."

Jassy ran Amazon Web Services before he became CEO in July 2021 . Bezos stayed on as executive chair.

Bezos' parting words to investors put the Day 1 mission squarely on his successor. "I guarantee you that Andy won't let the universe make us typical," he wrote in his last shareholder letter as CEO, published April 15, 2021.

Jassy is chasing a number nobody has hit

Under Jassy, staying in Day 1 has sometimes meant cutting. Amazon announced in October 2025 that it would eliminate about 14,000 corporate jobs. On the company's earnings call on Oct. 30, 2025, Jassy said the cuts weren't mainly about money or AI.

Fast growth meant "you end up with a lot more layers," Jassy said, adding, "We are committed to operating like the world's largest start-up."

He has also set a goal no company has ever reached.

"There has never been a trillion-dollar revenue business, and we may have two of them in the next 5-10 years," Jassy said in Amazon's third-quarter earnings release on Oct. 29. The two businesses he's betting on are Amazon's online stores and its cloud unit .

Third-quarter net sales rose 12% to $201.9 billion, and Amazon Web Services sales grew 39% to $46 billion, according to the release. Wall Street still wasn't fully convinced, and shares slid after the report as investors weighed how much Amazon is spending to get there.

Nobody at Amazon is shopping for funeral flowers yet. The company has already outlived the timeline its founder gave it. Bezos' bankruptcy prediction still stands, and every customer-obsessed year Jassy adds is another year Bezos gets to be wrong.

news.Title: Amazon.com vs. Home Depot: Which Consumer Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
news.Content:
How do you choose between a technology titan and a physical retail leader? Both Amazon.com (NASDAQ:AMZN) and Home Depot (NYSE:HD) offer investors unique exposure to consumer spending patterns and logistics expertise.

Amazon.com relies on its massive scale and digital ecosystem to drive growth across retail and cloud computing. Home Depot focuses on the home improvement market, serving both casual DIYers and professional trade specialists. This comparison helps you evaluate which strategy offers the best potential for the coming years.

The case for Amazon.com

Amazon.com operates a vast ecosystem that includes online and physical stores, third-party seller services, and advertising. The company serves a diverse customer base ranging from individual shoppers to large enterprises seeking cloud computing through Amazon Web Services. Its business model relies heavily on a network of third-party sellers and suppliers, many of which are based in China, to maintain its broad inventory.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached nearly $797.5 billion. This performance represents revenue growth of approximately 15.4% compared to the previous twelve-month period. Net income reached about $134.8 billion, but roughly $69 billion of that came from non-operating items, mostly gains on its private AI investments.

Based on its December 2025 balance sheet, the current ratio is approximately 1.1x. This metric measures a company's ability to meet its short-term liabilities using assets that can be converted to cash within a year. The debt-to-equity ratio is about 0.4x, indicating the relationship between total debt and shareholders' equity. In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, free cash flow was negative roughly $47 billion, as equipment purchases outpaced operating cash flow.

The case for Home Depot

Home Depot is the leading name among retail stocks focused on home improvement. The company serves do-it-yourself consumers and professional contractors, such as general contractors and trade specialists. Following its acquisition of SRS, the company has expanded its specialized distribution capabilities to better serve the complex needs of professional building product customers.

In the 12 months ended Nov. 1, 2026, revenue reached approximately $171.2 billion. This represents revenue growth of nearly 3% as the company navigates shifts in consumer spending on home projects. Net income during the same period was roughly $14.3 billion, demonstrating steady profitability despite a slower growth environment than the technology sector.

Story Continues

As of its February 2026 balance sheet, the current ratio is approximately 1.1x. The debt-to-equity ratio is roughly 5.1x, indicating the level of debt used to finance assets relative to shareholders' equity. In the fiscal year ended Feb. 1, 2026, free cash flow was close to $12.6 billion, providing the company with substantial cash to fund operations and shareholder returns.

Risk profile comparison

Amazon.com faces intense global competition across retail and cloud computing from well-funded rivals. The company must navigate evolving international regulations and geopolitical tensions, particularly regarding its operations in China and India. Operational risks include the complexity of its fulfillment network and data centers, where failures can cause significant disruptions. Additionally, the company faces legal risks from ongoing antitrust and consumer protection investigations that could impact its business practices.

Home Depot is highly sensitive to fluctuations in the housing market and interest rates, which directly influence demand for home improvement. The company faces operational risks related to the integration of large-scale strategic acquisitions like SRS and GMS. It is also subject to reputational risks from class action litigation, including legal challenges regarding AI-powered surveillance in store parking lots. Intense competition from both traditional and digital retailers requires the company to manage its aging store base while advancing its digital strategy.

Valuation comparison

Amazon.com looks more attractive based on future earnings estimates, while Home Depot offers a lower entry point based on trailing sales.

Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

The Forward P/E ratio compares a stock's current price to its expected earnings per share over the next year. Meanwhile, the P/S ratio measures the market capitalization of the company against its sales over the past twelve months.

Which stock would I buy for 2027?

The differentiator is how far each business can stretch. Home Depot sells to people building and fixing homes, and no matter how well it executes, that stays the ceiling. Even its SRS and GMS deals deepen the same building-products footprint. Amazon already earns from retail, cloud, advertising, and subscriptions, and it keeps adding bets, including a satellite network and a pending Globalstar deal. AWS grew 39% last quarter, which shows how much room the compute side still has.

The ride will be rougher. Amazon spends more cash than it generates, funds the gap with debt, and says capex will climb again in 2027. Investors will sit through stretches when the numbers look worse before they improve, and the stock can swing hard along the way. The thesis breaks only if demand for compute dries up, and that outcome would hit far more than one stock. I would buy Amazon for 2027 as a long-term holding, sized so a few bumpy years do not force a sale. Investors who want steady income and a smoother path should look at Home Depot instead.

news.Title: 台股崩7641點最慘一週！喊「現金為王」太晚？
news.Content:
台股上週暴跌7,641點、跌幅17.5%，收在36,033.29點，寫下史上最大單週跌點。融資餘額11月20日單日驟減491.41億元，五個交易日合計減少逾千億元，整戶維持率一路下探至156.18%，跌破160%。美股同日賣壓再度升溫，費城半導體指數暴跌10.73%，台積電ADR收跌9.36%，輝達（NVDA）受高層動盪與傳出遭SEC調查拖累，單日再挫近14%，那斯達克指數離20%熊市標準僅一步之遙。本週一至三，台股得同時消化美股補跌與融資追繳賣壓，36,000點能否守住備受關注；後市能否止跌，端看市場傳聞的財經部會「第三波護盤措施」、融資降幅是否趨緩，以及下週美國PCE物價指數對利率預期的影響。

AI熱潮降溫、通膨居高不下　黃金與日圓皆未能接棒

《鏈新聞》分析，資金面緊縮之際，機構法人為補足股市保證金，被迫出清變現容易的資產，使得原本被視為避險首選的黃金同遭賣壓，再加上高實質利率與美元強勢，金價同步回檔並回測3,500美元關卡。日圓在極端恐慌時，確實可能因套利交易平倉（Carry Trade Unwind）而急速升值，不過平時價格震盪明顯，美日利差也仍然偏大，難以充當穩定的避風港。

美債重回避險行列　但PCE是最大變數

至於美國中長天期公債，在避險買盤湧入下，10年期殖利率本週回到5%以下，避險角色有所恢復。分析提醒，短線殖利率仍將隨本週公布的PCE通膨數據波動。綜合各類資產的流動性與價格波動幅度，現金及短天期貨幣市場基金，目前最能提供低波動的防守空間。

「現金為王」現在才喊晚了嗎？　機構：這是為抄底備彈

市場也在討論，此時才強調「現金為王」是否已落後一步。《鏈新聞》彙整多數機構看法，認為這屬於「控管風險、調整資金部位」的過渡階段，並非從此退出市場。隨著AI題材的投資重心，從高估值的硬體基礎建設（「賣鏟子」），逐步轉向防禦型類股與體質穩健的公司，持有較高比重的現金與短天期債券，主要是為了避免在斷頭賣壓最猛烈時被迫停損認賠。等到融資強制賣壓告一段落、權值龍頭股止穩不再創低，且美股面對利空的反應逐漸麻痺，手上的現金便可望成為承接錯殺優質標的的資金來源。

news.Title: AI debt fears mount: why cash and defensive stocks are back in favor
news.Content:
Steep drops from all-time highs can make fallen tech leaders look cheap, particularly after a market leader has declined sharply from its high. But a lower stock price doesn't mean the industry's heavy financial bets will pay off — or that the broader market selloff is over.

Ron Insana, CEO of Insana Information Partners, is encouraging investors with heavy tech exposure to rebalance their portfolios, raise cash, and wait for clearer market signals. He suggests parking cash in three- and six-month U.S. Treasury bills for the time being, and favors companies like Berkshire Hathaway , Apple , Microsoft , and J. M. Smucker over the debt-heavy parts of the AI trade.

That strategy is intended for investors with overly concentrated portfolios or near-term cash needs. For long-term, buy-and-hold investors who have retirement money and decades before they plan to tap their funds, Insana takes a different view.

Here is how Insana, who spoke in an interview with TheStreet's Caroline Woods, separates near-term liquidity needs from long-term exposure to technology and stocks.

Why the S&P 500 can mask a deeper stock market decline

Insana's immediate concern is that major market indexes can look far healthier than the average stock. Since momentum peaked in June, he noted, roughly 40% to 50% of S&P 500 companies have fallen by 20% or more — the measure of an individual stock entering bear market territory — even while the broader index held up relatively well.

Insana argues that weakness spreads from the bottom up. If financial and tech shares falter as more stocks are already falling, the large-cap companies propping up the major indexes could be next. Still, he notes this is only a possibility. He acknowledged that his bearish call in March was wrong because the economy and market proved far more resilient than he anticipated.

For investors whose index funds have outperformed their individual stocks, Insana suggested trimming some S&P 500 exposure to reduce risk without panic-selling

the stocks that have already fallen. He frames the move not as an all-or-nothing market call, but as routine rebalancing to bring a portfolio back in line with an investor's risk tolerance.

Why AI debt matters more than a lower Nvidia share price

Insana, a former anchor on CNBC, sees the central risk in AI financing rather than in a single stock's valuation. He pointed to uncertainty over whether data-center revenue and return on invested capital, or the profit produced by money put into a business, will be sufficient to support the debt used to build AI infrastructure. He also cited growing losses at OpenAI and Anthropic despite rapidly rising revenue.

Story Continues

For Insana, a former CNBC anchor, the real threat isn't any individual stock's valuation — it's how AI is being financed. He flagged doubts over whether data-center revenue and return on invested capital — the profit earned on money put into the business — will cover the debt taken on to build AI infrastructure, noting that OpenAI and Anthropic face widening losses even as their revenues soar.

I think the bubble's on the debt side, not the equity side.

Insana was concerned that commitments can prove less durable in a downturn than investors expect. Beyond the $1.3 trillion in debt sitting on the balance sheets of hyperscalers and other companies, he pointed to $4 trillion in off-balance-sheet liabilities, such as leases and chip-purchase agreements. These obligations don't show up as standard debt.

That thesis helps explain why Insana isn't rushing to buy Nvidia just because the stock has dropped roughly 38% from its peak. He also pointed to legal and export-control uncertainties surrounding Nvidia's Blackwell chips. More broadly, he emphasized that a company with a strong long-term business can still suffer a severe downturn during a tech bust. He cited Amazon's 95% decline after the dot-com bubble burst in 2000 before it became one of the world's largest companies.

Why Insana favors Treasury bills and selected defensive stocks

When parking cash temporarily, Insana prefers three- or six-month U.S. Treasury bills — short-term government debt that were yielding roughly 3% to 4% at the time of the interview. The intention isn't to hold cash as a permanent strategy, he explained, but to keep funds liquid while waiting for clearer market signals.

His stock picks come down to different strengths on the balance sheet and in the underlying businesses. He pointed out that Microsoft was still producing positive free cash flow — the money left over after covering operating and capital expenses. At the same time, Apple hadn't committed the same level of spending on AI infrastructure. Berkshire Hathaway is his top pick because of its massive $370 billion cash hoard, which gives CEO Greg Abel plenty of flexibility to snap up bargains. As for J. M. Smucker, Insana sees it as a steady, countertrend defensive stock that could become a takeover target.

Still, those picks are no guarantee that defensive stocks will climb during a broad market downturn. Rather, they illustrate how Insana separated companies with strong cash generation and financial flexibility from those heavily reliant on ongoing, debt-funded AI spending. He also dismissed Bitcoin as a safe haven, noting it failed to hold up as one during the selloff.

The takeaway for investors weighing AI exposure and cash needs

For your portfolio, start by dividing your portfolio based on purpose: long-term investing, a near-term expense, or a tactical cash reserve — and keep those buckets separate. Under Insana's framework, long-term buy-and-hold investors should not let a market correction alone derail a retirement plan, whereas those actively drawing down funds should consider scaling back their stock exposure.

Next, evaluate your portfolio's concentration and time horizon. If technology holdings make up the bulk of your investments, rebalancing can help limit losses from a prolonged downturn. For cash earmarked for a home down payment or near-term living expenses, Insana's rule is straightforward: keep it out of the stock market. Going forward, monitor whether AI revenues, cash flows, borrowing costs, and broader credit-market stress support or challenge the broader thesis.

news.Title: 不是0050！台股崩萬點　它單週規模增逾12％稱霸
news.Content: 台股呈現高檔震盪格局，不過資金動能並未明顯降溫，被動台股ETF近一周規模增加5.8億元，部分人氣台股ETF規模亦有2~12%的成長。11月上旬台股迎來一波快速修正，加權指數自10月6日收盤的49,822.55點一路走低，11月6日單日重挫1,873.08點、收在39,701.64點，一個月內修正約20.3%，儘管指數隨後展開反彈，但11月中旬再逢黃仁勳辭去輝達執行長一事，為市場增添不確定性。 市場震盪之際，投資人仍有逢低承接、分批佈局的意願。目前市場上被動台股ETF規模破千億的有11檔。其中，近一周最受資金青睞的分別為國泰台灣科技龍頭(00881)及凱基台灣TOP50(009816)，兩者規模皆有逾12%的增長，可見投資人對其信心；元大台灣50(0050)、富邦台50(006208)，及富邦科技(0052)亦有雙位數規模成長、表現不俗。 法人指出，10月以來市場接連受到美國期中選舉及11月中旬換帥事件干擾，政治與人事面的非經濟事件放大短線市場情緒。儘管近一周人氣被動台股ETF皆成現正成長，但將時間拉長到11月以來觀察，在股市修正壓力下，僅凱基台灣TOP50(009816)、元大台灣50(0050)規模逆勢呈現正成長，顯示在股市修正之際，資金對市值型ETF布局動能仍具一定韌性。 近一個多月的兩波衝擊，一次來自政治結果引發的監管疑慮，一次來自人事更替引發的治理折價，性質都屬於評價修正，而不是由訂單減少引發的基本面衝擊。凱基台灣TOP50(009816)ETF研究團隊表示，台灣10月出口總額首度突破900億美元、第三季經濟成長率概估14.36%、雲端業者剩餘履約義務持續擴大，官方與企業數據都顯示AI需求仍以合約與產能的形式落地。短期波動難免，建議投資人透過定期定額策略，長線掌握AI成長機會。

news.Title: Alphabet vs. Meta Platforms: Which Media Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
news.Content:
Deciding between Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL) (NASDAQ:GOOG) and Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) means weighing the dominance of global search against a massive social media ecosystem in a transformative era for digital advertising.

Both companies are central to the modern internet, generating most of their revenue from digital ads. While Alphabet relies on its search engine and cloud services, Meta focuses on connecting billions of users through social apps. Investors often compare them to see which tech giant manages its growth and regulatory hurdles more effectively.

The case for Alphabet

Alphabet is a major player among communication stocks , primarily selling advertising space through Google Search and YouTube. Its customer base consists of advertisers and digital publishers, but it also depends on partners for hardware distribution and infrastructure leasing. Recent strategies focus heavily on integrating artificial intelligence across its entire product suite to maintain its leadership in information discovery and enterprise cloud services.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached nearly $471.1 billion, representing approximately 22.2% growth over the prior period. The company reported net income of nearly $235.7 billion during the same timeframe. This growth highlights the steady expansion of its search business and the successful scaling of its cloud operations as more businesses adopt digital tools.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is roughly 0.1x, which compares total debt to shareholder equity. A current ratio of nearly 2.0x indicates the company has $2.00 in current assets for every $1.00 in short-term liabilities. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was approximately $73.3 billion, which is the cash remaining after paying for operating costs and capital investments.

The case for Meta Platforms

Meta Platforms generates the vast majority of its revenue from marketers who advertise on its family of apps, including Facebook and Instagram. The company relies on content creators and developers who build on its platforms, as well as distribution partners like Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL). Its current focus involves investing heavily in AI to create new ways for people to connect digitally and improve the efficiency of its advertising systems.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached nearly $241.6 billion, fueled by revenue growth of approximately 27.5% over the previous year. Meta reported net income of roughly $75.2 billion during this timeframe. These results show strong engagement across its social apps even as the company navigates shifts in how users consume media and how marketers reach their target audiences.

Story Continues

On its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is roughly 0.4x, calculated by dividing total liabilities by shareholder equity. The current ratio is close to 2.6x, suggesting a strong ability to cover short-term debts with current assets. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was approximately $46.1 billion, representing the cash generated after spending on the necessary equipment and infrastructure to run its massive data centers.

Risk profile comparison

Alphabet faces significant competitive threats from established companies and emerging start-ups in advertising, artificial intelligence, and cloud services. Ongoing regulatory scrutiny and antitrust litigation involving government agencies pose material risks to its search and advertising practices. The company is also vulnerable to supply chain disruptions affecting critical infrastructure and to the risks posed by rapid technology shifts that could render current products less relevant.

Meta Platforms faces intense competition from other social platforms, as well as risks related to the evolution of the metaverse, which remains unproven and capital-intensive. Significant regulatory and legal risks include ongoing lawsuits over privacy and social media addiction, as well as strict compliance requirements under global frameworks. The company is also subject to revenue concentration in advertising and volatility from privacy-related changes implemented by mobile platform providers.

Valuation comparison

Alphabet looks cheaper by its Forward P/E using future earnings estimates, while Meta Platforms has a lower P/S ratio measuring sales over the past twelve months.

Which stock would I buy for 2027?

Alphabet's edge is that people and companies already run on it, and no single product depends on it. Search, YouTube, Android, and Chrome are part of daily habits, while Google Cloud sells to enterprises that sign multiyear contracts. Meta's apps reach huge audiences, but advertising funds nearly everything the company does, including a $25 billion New Mexico penalty it plans to appeal. Alphabet faces its own antitrust cases, and a bad ruling would hurt, but the damage would spread to more businesses. That breadth is why I'd buy Alphabet for the long term. Don't read its cheaper forward P/E as a bargain signal, because its reported earnings include investment gains that won't repeat. Meta fits investors who want faster ad growth and are willing to accept the legal overhang. If you plan to hold for years, build the position gradually and watch free cash flow, which turned negative over the first nine months of 2026 as AI spending climbed.

news.Title: Missed the First AI Rally? 5 Oversold Stocks With 50%+ Upside Potential
news.Content: The AI boom has rewarded early investors handsomely, but the opportunity now looks considerably less straightforward. After months of enthusiasm surrounding artificial intelligence, investors are increasingly questioning whether the enormous spending behind the technology can generate adequate returns. According to Reuters on November 19, the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index had lost nearly 30% since early October, even as estimates for major technology companies' capital expenditure remained largely unchanged. Barclays strategists noted that hyperscaler spending forecasts for next year had yet to be revised downward, suggesting that the market's retreat has outpaced changes in investment expectations. However, the concerns extend beyond valuations. Rising financing costs, regulatory uncertainty, and potential restrictions on data center construction have complicated the outlook. As examined in our coverage of AI infrastructure opportunities and financing risks following CoreWeave's earnings , strong demand alone cannot eliminate the financial risks associated with rapid expansion. Could the Selloff Offer a Second Opportunity? Wall Street, however, remains remarkably optimistic. Reuters reported on November 18 that 83% of analyst ratings on key AI stocks were Strong Buy recommendations, despite mounting concerns over profitability and debt. Yet Bank of America's November fund manager survey revealed a contrasting picture: nearly 40% of respondents believed companies were overinvesting, while more than half anticipated at least one hyperscaler cutting capital expenditure within six months. This divergence complicates the investment case. As explored in our earlier examination of oversold AI stocks with substantial analyst upside , falling share prices can widen implied returns without necessarily improving fundamentals. Meanwhile, our analysis of AI infrastructure stocks facing growing short-seller skepticism highlights another dimension of the risks accompanying that opportunity. For investors who missed the initial rally, the correction may offer another entry point. The challenge is distinguishing companies whose growth prospects remain intact from those whose valuations have further to fall. So, which oversold AI stocks offer the most attractive upside potential right now? We have compiled an expanded list of 10 Oversold AI Stocks With 50%+ Upside Potential, available here . The top five stocks from our list are presented below. Source: Seagate Our Methodology To compile our list, we screened U.S.-listed companies with exposure to AI through chips, cloud computing, software, or supporting infrastructure. We selected stocks that had declined by at least 25% over the preceding month and offered at least 50% upside to their median analyst price targets, using data as of November 20, 2026. Here, "oversold" refers to the size of the recent decline; we did not apply RSI or other technical indicators. Story Continues To offer readers additional ideas, we excluded stocks covered in our earlier list of oversold stocks , replacing overlapping names with the next-highest-upside qualifying companies. The final ten are presented in ascending order of analyst upside potential. We also considered hedge fund interest as of the third quarter of 2026, using Insider Monkey's hedge fund database, which tracked 994 hedge funds during the quarter. By the way billionaire Stan Druckenmiller issued a major warning about cybersecurity stocks. You can watch the video below: 5. Ciena Corporation (NYSE: CIEN ) Upside Potential: 104.30% 1M Decline: 27.95% Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 83 Ciena Corporation (NYSE:CIEN) supplies optical networking technology that connects AI data centers. The company made our list following a 27.95% monthly decline, with its median analyst price target implying 104.30% upside as of November 20. AI clusters need faster connections as computing workloads spread across multiple locations. That creates demand for equipment that carries more data without proportionately increasing power consumption. Ciena Corporation is already translating this demand into earnings: fiscal third-quarter revenue rose 37% to $1.67 billion, while adjusted operating margin reached 22.5%, compared with 10.7% a year earlier. Management expected fiscal year-end backlog to exceed $10 billion. The opportunity is substantial, but component availability limits how quickly orders become revenue. Its Hyper-Rail optical platform, designed to support distributed AI training, should begin contributing meaningful revenue during fiscal 2027. Ciena Corporation trades at approximately 22.1 times estimated fiscal 2027 earnings, with consensus anticipating roughly 66% EPS growth. That makes execution essential to the valuation. On November 16, TD Cowen retained its Buy rating while reducing its target to $375 from $400, arguing that strong demand made substantial near-term earnings estimate cuts difficult to justify. As explored in our earlier analysis of whether Ciena's growing AI backlog justifies its valuation premium , accelerating demand has raised expectations for sustained earnings growth. For Ciena Corporation, the stronger evidence would be continued backlog conversion and margin expansion, rather than the size of the implied upside alone. 4. Tower Semiconductor Ltd. (NASDAQ: TSEM ) Upside Potential: 111.30% 1M Decline: 39.38% Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 49 Tower Semiconductor Ltd. (NASDAQ:TSEM) manufactures silicon photonics and analog chips used in AI connectivity. Shares fell 39.38% over the past month, while the median analyst price target implied 111.30% upside as of November 20. Optical connections are becoming increasingly important as AI systems move more data between processors and facilities. Tower Semiconductor Ltd. generated approximately $240 million in silicon photonics revenue during the third quarter, nearly half its total. Overall revenue increased 33% to $526 million, while net income reached $120 million. Fourth-quarter revenue guidance of $600 million points to further growth. Capacity expansion looks to be the next test. Management expects silicon photonics manufacturing capacity at year-end to approximately double the level supporting third-quarter shipments. However, additional production capacity takes time to become recognized revenue, making the pace of customer ramps critical. Tower Semiconductor Ltd. trades at approximately 18.2 times estimated 2027 earnings, against projected EPS growth of roughly 72%. On November 3, Craig-Hallum maintained its Buy rating while cutting its target to $250 from $325, highlighting strong photonics demand and capacity expansion running ahead of schedule. Our earlier analysis of Tower Semiconductor's growing opportunities in AI optical connectivity highlighted how advances in silicon photonics could support higher-volume production, although scaling manufacturing remains a key challenge. Tower Semiconductor Ltd. has a sizable cash cushion, with approximately $1.47 billion in cash against $154 million in debt, supporting expansion while reducing its dependence on external financing. 3. Lumentum Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ: LITE ) Upside Potential: 111.60% 1M Decline: 40.75% Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 122 Lumentum Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ:LITE) makes our list after a 40.75% monthly decline, with its median analyst target implying 111.60% upside. Its lasers, optical transceivers, and switches help move data between AI processors, addressing bandwidth constraints as computing clusters expand. Lumentum Holdings Inc. reported fiscal first-quarter revenue of $1.26 billion and a 42.3% adjusted operating margin. Management also secured purchase commitments exceeding $5 billion for a second major win in optics positioned near or alongside chips. Next-quarter revenue guidance of $1.575–$1.625 billion suggests demand remains strong despite the selloff. However, Lumentum Holdings Inc. now carries acquisition risk alongside its operating opportunity. Under the proposed transaction, shareholders would receive 4.5 Marvell shares per share owned. The consideration therefore fluctuates with Marvell's stock, while completion remains subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals. The announced $1,132 equivalent is not a guaranteed cash payout. At approximately 21.5 times estimated fiscal 2027 earnings, Lumentum Holdings Inc. offers a lower earnings multiple than before the selloff, but growth and deal completion still matter. Our earlier examination of whether Lumentum can turn unmet demand into earnings that justify its valuation explores the operating challenge. UBS maintained Neutral on November 10, noting accelerating optical demand but identifying the acquisition as the principal near-term share-price driver. Short interest stood at 8.97% of float on October 30, before the deal announcement. 2. Marvell Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ: MRVL ) Upside Potential: 118.80% 1M Decline: 45.29% Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 108 Marvell Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ:MRVL) qualifies following a 45.29% monthly decline, with 118.80% upside to its median analyst target. Its custom processors, networking chips, and optical connectivity products support AI systems whose performance increasingly depends on moving data efficiently. Marvell Technology, Inc. generated $2.17 billion in fiscal second-quarter data-center revenue, up 46% year-over-year. In November, preliminary third-quarter revenue remained consistent with its earlier guidance. That distinction matters: the selloff reflects concerns about future spending and acquisition execution, rather than an announced quarterly revenue shortfall. The proposed Lumentum acquisition would give Marvell Technology, Inc. greater control over the lasers and optical components that complement its chips. However, integrating a manufacturing-intensive business introduces customer conflicts and regulatory uncertainty. Expected completion in the first half of 2028 leaves considerable time before the combined business can demonstrate its benefits. Marvell Technology, Inc. trades at approximately 32.8 times estimated fiscal 2027 earnings and 18.8 times fiscal 2028 earnings. That lower later-year multiple depends on substantial profit growth. Our analysis of whether its $20 billion fiscal 2028 revenue ambition can justify the valuation examines the expectations behind that opportunity. Stifel retained Buy on November 20 while reducing its target to $280 from $370. The continued endorsement supports the growth case, but the target reduction reinforces why a sharp decline alone does not establish undervaluation. 1. Sandisk Corporation (NASDAQ: SNDK ) Upside Potential: 164.80% 1M Decline: 49.87% Sandisk Corporation (NASDAQ:SNDK) enters our list after a 49.87% monthly decline, with 164.80% upside to its median analyst target. Its NAND flash and solid-state drives provide storage for AI workloads, including the expanding information that inference systems must retain and retrieve. Sandisk Corporation reported fiscal first-quarter revenue of $11.03 billion, up 23% sequentially. Data-center revenue increased 61% sequentially to approximately $4.8 billion. Management attributed roughly 60% of total sequential revenue growth to volume and 40% to pricing, indicating that the expansion was not solely a pricing story. Long-term customer agreements could make Sandisk Corporation's earnings more predictable by improving visibility into demand. On November 11, Evercore maintained Outperform, arguing that supply discipline and these agreements could support more durable profitability. Our coverage of why Evercore sees more resilience in Sandisk's NAND business examines that argument. Sandisk Corporation also returned $5 billion through quarterly buybacks and projected next-quarter revenue of $12.2–$12.6 billion. Repurchases can increase remaining shareholders' participation in future earnings, provided the company preserves sufficient cash for technology investment. The main question is how much profitability survives a weaker memory market. An 85.1% adjusted gross margin leaves substantial room for normalization, and management urged caution when modeling the seasonally softer March quarter. AI demand strengthens the investment case, but investors still need earnings that endure beyond today's favorable supply conditions. While we acknowledge the risk and potential of SNDK as an investment, we believe certain AI infrastructure stocks offer far stronger long-term potential at a much more attractive entry point. If you are looking for an AI stock more promising than SNDK that operates as a critical AI tollbooth and stands as the most important company in the world, check out our report about this must-own AI stock . news.Title: Walmart's Sam's Club adds a deal Costco can't copy
news.Content: For a deal to be worth it, you have to actually want the products being discounted. Pepsi, for example, could send me free coupons and Subway could email me a massive gift card, and I wouldn't take advantage of either because I don't like the underlying products. Walmart's new bundled membership brings customers a Sam's Club Plus membership and a Walmart+ membership for $120. That's an $88 savings over buying them separately, and essentially only a $22 upcharge over the $98 Walmart membership, which will make the deal attractive for Walmart members. As a Costco fan who orders from Amazon nearly every day, however, I can't see the value enticing me to make a change. A quick look at Walmart's pricing Walmart's bundle gives customers access to Sam's Club with 2% cash back, along with free shipping, the choice between Paramount+ Essential (with ads) and Peacock Premium (with ads), and the other Walmart+ benefits. The pricing makes it an easy choice for anyone who might use both. Walmart+: $98 per year or $12.95 per month Sam's Club Plus: $110 per year Sam's Club membership (standard): $50 per year Walmart's bundle: $120 for Walmart+ and Sam's Club Plus Walmart is bullish on the bundle Walmart CEO John Furner pushed the new bundle hard during the retailer's third-quarter earnings call . "Each membership, Sam's Club Plus and Walmart+, is valuable on its own. Bundling them lets us do more for the same household while helping them save on the combined cost. We think about it this way: a delivery membership, a warehouse club, and a streaming service can add up to nearly $400 a year," he shared. The problem, however, is that, at least for me, Costco trumps Sam's Club, and Amazon is superior to Walmart.com. Amazon Prime also has like five of my favorite shows, while Paramount+ has none, and Peacock has "SNL" and "Law & Order" reruns when I forget to set my DVR. More Walmart: Walmart faces FTC scrutiny over AI-era personalized pricing Walmart has a new plan to solve one of its customers' biggest problems Walmart copies a core Costco move that also benefits customers A Costco Executive membership costs $130 per year, while Amazon Prime charges $139 a year and includes Prime Video. That's $120 for Walmart's bundle versus $269 for Amazon and Costco, but for the Walmart deal to offer value, you have to actually want to shop at Sam's, order from Walmart.com, and find something to watch on Paramount+ or Peacock. Will Costco lose members to Walmart? Retail expert Maurie Backman, a Costco member, thinks this deal could help Walmart add members. Story Continues "I wouldn't switch to Sam's Club and ditch Costco based on price, but I'd consider joining Sam's Club on top of Costco if it was cheap enough and I felt it offered something Costco didn't," she told TheStreet. The deal, however, could bring more Walmart customers to Sam's Club. "Consumer Edge data shows that nearly 70% of Walmart shoppers haven't made a purchase at Sam's Club over the past year. In fact, almost half haven't purchased from any of the three major warehouse clubs: Sam's Club, Costco Wholesale, or BJ's Wholesale Club," according to the report . Offering a cheap way into the Sam's Club door could be a driver for the warehouse club chain. "With consumers continuing to prioritize value and convenience, this could be another example of Walmart looking beyond price alone to strengthen customer loyalty and capture a greater share of household spending," added Consumer Edge. Walmart bets on membership Membership fee revenue grew 17% globally in Q3, according to CFO John David Rainey. "As John mentioned, we are encouraged by the response to our new U.S. bundled membership offering, with strong new member sign-ups and upgraded memberships running well ahead of our expectations," he shared during the earnings call. news.Title: Sam's Club made a change Costco can't copy
news.Content: For a deal to be worth it, you have to actually want the products being discounted. Pepsi, for example, could send me free coupons and Subway could email me a massive gift card, and I wouldn't take advantage of either because I don't like the underlying products. Walmart's new bundled membership brings customers a Sam's Club Plus membership and a Walmart+ membership for $120. That's an $88 savings over buying them separately, and essentially only a $22 upcharge over the $98 Walmart membership, which will make the deal attractive for Walmart members. As a Costco fan who orders from Amazon nearly every day, however, I can't see the value enticing me to make a change. A quick look at Walmart's pricing Walmart's bundle gives customers access to Sam's Club with 2% cash back, along with free shipping, the choice between Paramount+ Essential (with ads) and Peacock Premium (with ads), and the other Walmart+ benefits. The pricing makes it an easy choice for anyone who might use both. Walmart+: $98 per year or $12.95 per month Sam's Club Plus: $110 per year Sam's Club membership (standard): $50 per year Walmart's bundle: $120 for Walmart+ and Sam's Club Plus Walmart is bullish on the bundle Walmart CEO John Furner pushed the new bundle hard during the retailer's third-quarter earnings call . "Each membership, Sam's Club Plus and Walmart+, is valuable on its own. Bundling them lets us do more for the same household while helping them save on the combined cost. We think about it this way: a delivery membership, a warehouse club, and a streaming service can add up to nearly $400 a year," he shared. The problem, however, is that, at least for me, Costco trumps Sam's Club, and Amazon is superior to Walmart.com. Amazon Prime also has like five of my favorite shows, while Paramount+ has none, and Peacock has "SNL" and "Law & Order" reruns when I forget to set my DVR. More Walmart: Walmart faces FTC scrutiny over AI-era personalized pricing Walmart has a new plan to solve one of its customers' biggest problems Walmart copies a core Costco move that also benefits customers A Costco Executive membership costs $130 per year, while Amazon Prime charges $139 a year and includes Prime Video. That's $120 for Walmart's bundle versus $269 for Amazon and Costco, but for the Walmart deal to offer value, you have to actually want to shop at Sam's, order from Walmart.com, and find something to watch on Paramount+ or Peacock. Will Costco lose members to Walmart? Retail expert Maurie Backman, a Costco member, thinks this deal could help Walmart add members. Story Continues "I wouldn't switch to Sam's Club and ditch Costco based on price, but I'd consider joining Sam's Club on top of Costco if it was cheap enough and I felt it offered something Costco didn't," she told TheStreet. The deal, however, could bring more Walmart customers to Sam's Club. "Consumer Edge data shows that nearly 70% of Walmart shoppers haven't made a purchase at Sam's Club over the past year. In fact, almost half haven't purchased from any of the three major warehouse clubs: Sam's Club, Costco Wholesale, or BJ's Wholesale Club," according to the report . Offering a cheap way into the Sam's Club door could be a driver for the warehouse club chain. "With consumers continuing to prioritize value and convenience, this could be another example of Walmart looking beyond price alone to strengthen customer loyalty and capture a greater share of household spending," added Consumer Edge. Walmart bets on membership Membership fee revenue grew 17% globally in Q3, according to CFO John David Rainey. "As John mentioned, we are encouraged by the response to our new U.S. bundled membership offering, with strong new member sign-ups and upgraded memberships running well ahead of our expectations," he shared during the earnings call. He also gave a peek at just how big Walmart's plans are when it comes to membership "This was an important milestone in our journey to become the most essential membership program for consumers," he added. RTM Nexus CEO Dominick Miserandino thinks the Walmart deal will be enticing to some, but most members probably won't be Costco members who make the jump. "I think bundles do help. Think about how they are doing when it comes to cellphone plans. But, that said, I think loyalty always makes fans of brands," he told TheStreet. news.Title: 〈台股風向球〉連環套賣壓需時間換空間 長期投資人心態先穩住
news.Content:
台股過去一周湧出連鎖多殺多賣壓，共爆挫7641點、跌幅高達17.5%，金管會實施全面限空令，且上周五台積電最後一盤也湧現超過1萬張的買單，顯示國家隊全力護盤的意念，不過，法人提醒，上周五美股重挫令台股本周空頭巨浪持續席捲，融資斷頭恐全面殺出，籌碼要沉澱短期非易事，「長期投資人時間換取空間，個人心態先穩住」。

上周五台股爆發逃命賣壓，緊接著美股又重挫，法人不諱言，這波大盤修正恐比過去影響範圍更廣的原因在於─更多小資散戶「在船上」；由於對AI發展趨勢的強勁信心使拉回就有低接買盤，反而在現階段形成上檔重重連環套，而先無論投資金額大小，負面感受恐較以往更深刻，不過，內資已紛紛給出正向的鼓舞。

元大投顧分析，最新美銀美林基金經理人調查報告顯示，華爾街大砍科技股力道創20 年新高，反映 AI 投資帶進的收入難跟上資本支出投入速度，加上民主黨勝選後資料中心建置可能延宕或受限，造成股市本益比壓縮，因此，台股從逼近5萬點的 22 倍本益比，逐步下跌到 16.5倍本益比，重新回到過去合理區間 14-18 倍本益比當中。

不過，因調整仍在持續，布局上仍以降低槓桿與持股水位為優先，建議在行情未正式出現轉機訊息前勿貿然攤平。

永豐投顧分析，金管會祭出新的限空措施，使台股空方力道受到抑制，有助市場提早尋求短期平衡點，但因相關措施不利市場流動性，建議先觀望等待。

由於此次大盤重挫是涉及AI產業資本支出和CSP擴張策略調整，與過去單純因高槓桿操作所造成的修正有所不同，提防貿然搶反彈的風險。

短線先觀察美國國會已邀請黃仁勳在12月1日出席國會聽證，因聽證結果具高度不確定性，若聽證結果侷限於個人私德，或許對輝達影響有限，若是牽涉到晶片出口是否合規，則牽涉範圍廣泛。

2018年恐慌：清倉式 ...
